subject.title: [Feature]: Intelligent Model Fallback with Wildcard/Auto Selection

question: Should OpenClaw add a core provider-family model fallback contract for this issue, and if so should the public shape be wildcard/auto refs, explicit fallback families, catalog-derived fallbacks, or no new core config?
rationale: The issue is a valid provider-routing problem, but the remaining choice changes public config semantics and provider/auth fallback behavior, and the discussion already contains incompatible implementation shapes.

options.title: Define one core family-fallback contract
options.body: Approve a single public config shape and require implementation across schema, config normalization, fallback resolution, docs, and focused upgrade tests.

options.title: Keep only explicit flat fallbacks
options.body: Close or defer this issue if maintainers want provider-family policy to stay outside core and require users to maintain explicit fallback lists.

options.title: Route to plugin or policy hook work
options.body: Treat provider-family routing as external policy/plugin behavior only if a core extension seam can safely observe and influence fallback candidate selection.

recommendation.title: Define one core family-fallback contract
recommendation.body: Approve a single public config shape and require implementation across schema, config normalization, fallback resolution, docs, and focused upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Most of the central model fallback feature history and documentation provenance points to this owner as the best first routing point for the contract choice.
